Container.Name: hearth
Container.Overview: Self-hosted rooms for voice, screen sharing, OBS ingest and chat - a private living room for a handful of friends: open a channel, get a few people in, put your screen up. - Group voice forwarded by an SFU, with noise suppression, push-to-talk and auto-mute - 1080p60 screen sharing at a real bitrate, system audio included; the camera rides the same line - OBS pushes in over plain WHIP with no plugin; the stream is forwarded untouched, so HEVC and AV1 pass through - Chat with mentions, replies, reactions and direct file transfer - Passkey login, invite-only registration, per-channel roles One container holds all of it: API, media core, ingest endpoint and web UI. No redis, no second container, no separate media server to install. [b]Before you start: appdata ownership[/b] The image runs as uid 65532 (distroless nonroot), while Unraid creates appdata as nobody:users. Run this once in the Unraid terminal or the container will not be able to write its database: mkdir -p /mnt/user/appdata/hearth && chown -R 65532:65532 /mnt/user/appdata/hearth [b]After installing[/b] Create the first account from the Unraid terminal - it automatically becomes super admin: docker exec -it hearth /app/hearth adduser alice change-me [b]Certificate[/b] The web port also serves https. Other devices on the LAN must install the root certificate once at https://[IP]:[PORT:8080]/ca (plain http works too). Without it the browser will not grant microphone, screen share or notification permissions. [b]Media port[/b] 47720/udp must be open on your firewall, and the host port must keep the same number as the container port: the in-process media core writes the port it listens on into its ICE candidates, so a different host port would advertise an unreachable one. 47720/tcp is an ICE-TCP fallback, on by default at the same number.

Config.Name: Web UI
Config.Description: Web, API, signalling and WHIP share this one port, which also accepts https by default.

Config.Name: Media UDP
Config.Description: Media port for voice and screen sharing. Must be open on your firewall, and must keep the same number on host and container.

Config.Name: Media ICE-TCP
Config.Description: ICE-TCP fallback, only needed where UDP is intercepted by middleboxes. Same number as the UDP media port.

Config.Name: Data
Config.Description: The only persistence boundary: database, generated keys and the self-signed root certificate. Must be owned by uid 65532 - run chown -R 65532:65532 on it before first start.
